extracted.intended_audience: state and local air agencies, regulated industry, environmental stakeholders, and public commenters following EPA rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of Federal Register summaries of EPA actions and proposed/final rulemakings related to air pollution control (SIP approvals, NESHAP/NAAQS actions, delegations, state plans, etc.). Useful for stakeholders preparing comments or compliance plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP non-interference with attainment and reasonable further progress
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will approve a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision if it "will not interfere with any applicable requirement concerning attainment and reasonable further progress or any other applicable requirement of the Clean Air Act (CAA or Act)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the recurring legal standard used by EPA in evaluating SIP revisions; approvals typically assert that the revision does not interfere with attainment, RFP, or other CAA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attainment plan required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: An attainment plan must include the State's attainment demonstration and other elements required under the Clean Air Act, including emission limitations necessary to provide for attainment, base-year and projection-year emission inventories, reasonably available control measures and reasonably available control technology (RACM/RACT), nonattainment new source review (NNSR), requirements for meeting reasonable further progress (RFP), and contingency measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When EPA reviews an attainment plan (for a NAAQS), it checks for all these statutory components and evaluates whether the plan provides for attainment by the applicable deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Plans under CAA section 111(d) must implement Emissions Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Plan under section 111(d) must provide for implementation and enforcement of the Emissions Guidelines (EG) and Compliance Times applicable to the regulated source category and establish emission limits, monitoring, operating, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements for affected sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates whether the State Plan adopts the EG, sets appropriate limits, and includes required monitoring/recordkeeping and enforcement provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interstate transport / 'good neighbor' SIP obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SIP must contain adequate provisions prohibiting emissions that will significantly contribute to nonattainment or interfere with maintenance of air quality in other states for the applicable NAAQS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviews SIP submissions for their adequacy in addressing interstate transport (e.g., for PM2.5, ozone) and will approve if the State's provisions meet the 'significant contribution' and 'interfere with maintenance' obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal enforceability of emission reduction credit (ERC) programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs that allow generation of emission reduction credits (ERCs) by actions such as retrofitting or replacing fleet vehicles must establish ERCs as federally enforceable and meet Clean Air Act requirements to be used as offsets in Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates whether the ERC generation, quantification, and enforceability meet federal NNSR offset criteria before approving statewide or local programs into the SIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: RACT implementation for existing sources
rubrics_metrics.description: SIP revisions implementing statewide reasonably available control technology (RACT) requirements must limit emissions (e.g., NOx) from the relevant existing sources (for example, municipal waste combustors) as required to meet the NAAQS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA assesses whether the state's RACT determinations are consistent with CAA requirements and sufficiently implemented to ensure the NAAQS can be met and maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: State rule revisions should align definitions with federal definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: State regulatory definitions (for example, the regulatory definition of "volatile organic compound" (VOC)) should be amended to align with EPA's regulatory definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment avoids inconsistencies between state and federal law and is a common basis for EPA approval of SIP revisions that amend definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction permits program must ensure NAAQS attainment/maintenance and SIP consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to state construction permit requirement regulations (including fees, applicability subsections, administrative wording) must help ensure ambient air quality standards are met and must be properly reflected in the SIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA approves changes that maintain or improve the effectiveness of the permit program and that are consistent with previously approved SIP provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) excess emissions provisions must avoid prior deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to SIP provisions pertaining to periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction should amend provisions in a manner that avoids deficiencies previously identified by EPA (including those that led to disapproval actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should correct deficiencies identified in earlier EPA disapprovals; EPA reviews revised SSM provisions for compliance with CAA section 110 and implementing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA may find failure to attain and reclassify nonattainment areas
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA determines whether an area failed to attain the NAAQS by the attainment date and may reclassify area severity (e.g., from Moderate to Serious) if attainment was not achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of failure to attain trigger statutory obligations; EPA considers monitoring data, exceptional events, and other submissions when making determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of exceptional events and international emissions in attainment determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may consider exceptional events requests and emissions emanating from outside the U.S. when determining whether an area attained the NAAQS by the attainment date (e.g., determine area would have attained but for international emissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may submit exceptional events demonstrations; EPA will concur or not and may account for international transport in its attainment/reclassification decisions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority to implement federal plans requires enforceability and clear scope
rubrics_metrics.description: When a state or local agency requests delegation to implement and enforce a Federal plan (e.g., for affected Sewage Sludge Incineration units or partial delegation of CAA 112(r) RMP), EPA will codify approval if the delegation provides for implementation/enforcement; EPA may retain authority for sources or chemicals outside the delegated scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation approvals often specify retained EPA authorities and the boundaries of delegation (e.g., excluding sources that don't meet a statutory definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: NESHAP technology review requirements under CAA section 112
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA section 112 technology reviews assess existing NESHAP standards and may result in (a) no revisions, (b) proposals to regulate previously unregulated emission points, or (c) proposals to defer regulation of certain points; reviews may also propose definitional changes (e.g., "associated equipment") and technical corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's technology review analyzes control feasibility and statutory obligations; it may propose alternative approaches for unregulated emission points and consider impacts on regulated entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: State redesignation to attainment must meet statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to redesignate an area to attainment (e.g., for PM2.5) must demonstrate that the area meets the CAA criteria for redesignation, including attainment shown by monitoring data and applicable SIP requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will approve redesignations that satisfy the statutory prerequisites (attainment, maintenance plan, fully approved SIP, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: State rule revisions should remove duplicative language and streamline permitting where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: SIP revisions may revise thresholds of applicability, add incorporations by reference, add necessary definitions, remove unnecessarily restrictive or duplicative language, and add streamlined processes (for example, for vapor recovery modifications) while ensuring they do not interfere with attainment or maintenance of the NAAQS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA looks for clarity, consistency, and assurance that streamlined processes do not weaken substantive protection required by the CAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP approvals are conditioned on meeting relevant CAA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's proposed or final approvals explicitly state that the submission meets relevant CAA requirements and that the action is being taken pursuant to the Clean Air Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an overarching criterion: EPA evaluates SIPs and related state/local rules against all applicable CAA provisions and approving actions explain which requirements are met.
